FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Policies v3, as of August 31, 2026. Renter policy: FEMA marks the policyholder a tenant, the building residential, no building coverage and some contents coverage. Priced: a policy cost above $0. How we check them.

What does renters flood insurance cover?

An NFIP renters policy protects the things you own inside your home, such as furniture, clothes, televisions, computers, rugs and some artwork, for up to $100,000 of damage. It is contents coverage.

Most NFIP policies take effect 30 days after you buy, so a policy bought today will not cover a flood this week.

To buy: call the NFIP at (877) 336-2627, go to FloodSmart.gov, or ask any licensed insurance agent. Every NFIP insurer offers the same rates.

What it won't pay: The NFIP's standard policy for homes (the Dwelling Form) does not pay for a hotel or other living costs while you are out of the home, or for belongings outside the building, and it limits what it pays for in a basement. Belongings are paid at actual cash value (their used value), not the cost of new ones. The policy generally counts a flood only when water covers two or more acres of normally dry land or two or more properties, one of them yours.

What these numbers cannot tell you

Your premium, private insurers' prices, or why a price changed. The median is what existing NFIP renter policies pay, not a quote. Whether you must buy it is not in FEMA's data: only your lease or landlord can say.

Sources: FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP Policies v3; rules from ecfr.gov, floodsmart.gov, law.cornell.edu.
